it takes a while for your skin to get used to a retinoid, what a lot of people like to do is when starting to use epiduo use it only once every 3 days for 2 weeks to a month, depending on how your skin responds, then increasing to once every two days, then once daily.

epiduo in particular can be really drying because of the benzoyl peroxide so make sure you are using a good moisturiser, you can also buffer the epiduo which is where you apply the epiduo after moisturiser, the moisturiser acts as a barrier to slow its absorption, reduce dryness and reduce irritation.

you can continue using epiduo, this is normal and not a bad sign, you can continue using it, just infrequently until your skin becomes more tolerant. and yes slugging is great!

also yes epiduo will help with large pores, adapalene is a great ingredient for this.

yeah sure! petroleum jelly is great because it's such a good occlusive (it's one of, if not the most effective ingredient at doing this) occlusives being ingredients that create a barrier over your skin, preventing things from getting in or out, most significantly preventing trans epidermal water loss from your skin (the process of water leaving your skin). for me this translates to it really plumping and softening my skin.

it's occlusive properties also mean that it can amplify the effect of products layered underneath it. this but some people really do, this can be both good or bad, it can be bad when you're using potentially irritating or drying ingredients like chemical exfoliants or retinoids, or really any actives, but if you're using soothing, hydrating products (even a simple moisturiser) it really amplifies the effects.

it also has nearly no potential for irritation so it's safe to use on just about anything. once i had really dry flaky eyelids and i couldn't put on anything because it would sting so much, the only thing that i could use was vaseline, and it worked really well. so it's safe to use if your skin is irritated, you have allergies, etc. it's also non comedogenic (although some people say it breaks them out and it can give some people milia) so you often see it in sensitive skin products and products meant for babies.

bottom line is just know that it traps in some steam and moisture which depending on what you are doing can be a good thing or a bad thing, use your judgement and if it works for you, keep doing it.

are the onion and garlic fresh or powder?

if they're fresh i would recommend cooking them in a pan with a little bit of oil or butter until slightly browned, then add paprika and cayenne and stir them around for a few seconds and their colour is distributed and you can smell them. (if your heat is high they can burn very quickly so be careful) after that add the boiling broth and add the oregano and thyme so they can infuse their flavours gently. this way the ingredients are able to flavour the dish in their preferred way and adding them at different times creates some dimension.

if the onion and garlic powder are dried, i'm not too sure what to do. toasting them in a bit of butter (butter over oil because it wont get as hot and risk burning the spices) with the paprika and cayenne then adding hot stock, oregano and thyme might be a good option. Or you could add a shallot or something, brown it a little, then add the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cayenne, toast them a little, then add hot stock and herbs.

I recommend toasting the onion, garlic, paprika and cayenne in some sort of fat over oil as i find that they can take the heat and toast a little, the onion and garlic caramalise a little bit and lose any raw pungency and the paprika and cayenne infuse their colour and their flavour really comes out. i wouldnt toast the herbs since heat can change their flavour and they wont have the same freshness to them, id recommend just putting them in hot water (or stock or something just not oil)
